failed_output: A first pass of the classifier reported 253 lemmas as an "unconditioned retroflex residue" without flagging that tváṣṭar- (65 tokens) and táṣṭar- (7) head the list and are transparently from √takṣ-, where RUKI applies after k and the k is then lost in the cluster.
bias_or_method_failure: Method failure, not bias: a rule over a surface string cannot see a deleted conditioning segment, and the output was initially read as if it could.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: None. The failure is in the instrument, not in whose evidence was trusted.
correction: DME-014 records the two false positives explicitly and DME-004 is restated as an upper bound. The formal sub-typology F1–F4 was added so that the shapes in which internal derivations are likely are marked in the register itself.
future_control: Any mechanical phonological classifier in this repository states, in its own header, the derivations it cannot see, and its output is called an upper bound rather than a residue.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: None. This is the first mechanical phonological classification in the repository.

failed_output: A lemma-name search for hydronyms returned no Sarasvatī, no Paruṣṇī and no Asiknī, and would have supported a statement that the corpus does not name them.
bias_or_method_failure: Method failure of the same family as inherited correction C-04, in the opposite direction: C-04 was a stem search over-counting, this is a lemma search under-counting. Both mistake an annotation layer for the text.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: The Zurich/Grassmann lemmatisation is a modern editorial analysis. Treating its citation forms as the corpus's own inventory of names imports an editorial decision as if it were data.
correction: The census was rebuilt to match accent-stripped surface forms against an explicit name list, and every hit is typed by hand as RIVER, AMBIGUOUS, DERIVATIVE, REGION-OR-EPITHET or NOT-RIVER. DME-018 records the three lemmatisations that caused it.
future_control: No absence claim about a named entity in the Rigveda may rest on a lemma search alone. Surface search plus hand typing, or the claim does not get made.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: The púr- family unit (03-REGISTERS/rigveda-pur-family.csv) relies on the lemma layer for recall. Its own padapāṭha recall check partly covers this, but the check was for púr-, not for names. Queued as RA-001.

failed_output: The draft gating table initially recorded a specialist-standing verdict for Witzel's Para-Munda proposal and for the accepted-loan corpus, drawn from recollection rather than from a retrieved statement.
bias_or_method_failure: Prestige-bias in its purest form: a famous proposal was about to receive a characterisation, and therefore a standing, that no retrieval in this session supported.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: It assumed that a widely cited position is well enough known that summarising it is not the same as sourcing it. The inheritance rule says the opposite, and says it about exactly this material.
correction: Every current_specialist_standing cell for a blocked row now reads "Not sourced here", and the rows are typed NOT-ELIGIBLE-SOURCE-BLOCKED rather than given a verdict. HOLD-003 records what would be needed.
future_control: A standing verdict requires a retrieved statement with a locator. Where none exists the cell says so and the row gets no analytical space, in either direction.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: None in this repository yet. The failure the constitution §1 describes happened in prior chat threads and is inherited at INHERITED-UNVERIFIED.

failed_output: The flat distribution of the retroflex residue across Arnold's strata was first written up as "the residue does not accumulate through the Rigveda."
bias_or_method_failure: Preferred-counter-narrative failure, running against the counter-narrative rather than with it: a null result was being reported as a refutation of Kuiper-style accumulation claims, which is the corrective-sounding conclusion in this context and was reached on a weak proxy with limited power.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: It treated a measurement made on one diagnostic as though it settled a question about foreignness in general, and it did so in the direction that makes the canonical substrate account look worse.
correction: DME-010 now reports the trend statistic and its direction as part of the result: z = +1.28 in the predicted direction, p = 0.20. DME-020 is capped at PROVISIONAL with three stated reasons and says explicitly that a null is not a refutation.
future_control: Any null result in this repository reports the point estimate and its direction alongside the p-value, and states the power limitation, before it is allowed to bear on a hypothesis.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: PUR-026 in 03-REGISTERS/rigveda-pur-family.csv rests on a significant result rather than a null, but its second instrument returned a null that was reported as disagreement rather than as low power. Queued as RA-002.

stage: domain M / domain E interface, step 10 (bridge testing) and step 12 (falsifiers)
failed_output: A leave-one-out geographic measurement over attested Dravidian languages was interpreted as showing something about where Dravidian was spoken, and specifically as making Brahui's northwestern position anomalous and in need of a migration explanation. Recorded in full at DMB-001.
bias_or_method_failure: Method failure. A delete-one statistic computed over a set with one extreme member measures the influence of that member on the statistic. Reporting the remainder is a sensitivity report about the instrument. Converting it into a claim about a language family's geography is the step-10 bridge failure in its exact form: the link from 'the statistic moves a long way when this element is deleted' to 'this element is anomalous in the history' is a separate claim and was never made, let alone tested.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: It assumes that the set of attested Dravidian languages is a sample of Dravidian geography. It is a sample of survival. The languages attested today are the ones that were not replaced, and the archive that records them is the colonial and post-colonial survey record, which enumerated speech communities it reached and classified. Deleting Brahui does not simulate a Dravidian world without Brahui; it simulates the record we would hold if one more replacement had run to completion. Under the step-6 archive audit that is the whole question, and the statistic assumes it away.
affected_claims: DMB-001 (superseded), DMB-002 (restatement); bears on IH-135 / hypothesis H-01, IH-031, IH-156 / rejected row R-10; and on the reading of DME-022 and DME-023
correction: DMB-001 is SUPERSEDED and retained, not deleted. DMB-002 restates the claim to the two things the statistic can carry: the instrument's exposure to one datapoint, and the size of the gap between Brahui and the next-nearest attested Dravidian language. Unit 2 supplies the arithmetic (DMB-010 to DMB-013) by computing the delete-one influence of all twenty attested varieties, so that Brahui's influence is reported against a distribution rather than on its own.
future_control: No leave-one-out, jackknife or delete-one statistic in this repository is reported without (a) the per-element influence of every element, not only the element of interest, and (b) an explicit statement of the reference point or estimand and of who chose it. A delete-one result reported for one element alone is a sensitivity claim presented as a finding.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: The reading of DME-022 and DME-023 as bearing on donor-language geography. Those rows are corpus-internal and correctly scoped, but DME-023 states a compatibility with 'the greater Indus and north-west' whose own geographic reference point is not stated numerically. Queued as RA-004. Also the inherited rows IH-031, IH-135 and IH-156, which carry the burden-of-proof argument this measurement was being used inside; queued as RA-005.

stage: domain M, step 4 (evidence classes kept separate) and step 10 (bridge testing)
topic: North Dravidian subgrouping and the independence assumption
failed_output: A Euclidean distance from each attested Dravidian language to a northwestern reference point, with the languages treated as independent observations and Brahui read off as an isolated outlier.
bias_or_method_failure: Method failure with a bias consequence. A distance-to-reference statistic has no term for shared descent, so it cannot represent a clade. If Brahui, Kurukh and Malto subgroup, their three positions are not three observations; they are one observation of an ancestor's location plus whatever happened afterwards. Treating them as three both inflates the apparent support and makes Brahui look like it stands alone when it may be the northwestern member of a group that also reaches Jharkhand. A second and separate defect: Euclidean distance over a latitude/longitude pair is not a distance on the earth, and its error is a function of latitude, which is exactly the axis the northwest/south contrast runs along.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: The representation is not neutral. Rendering a language family as a scatter of points in a plane is the representation in which 'Brahui stands alone' is true by construction, because the representation has deleted the only structure - descent - that could make it not stand alone. Choosing that representation and then reading a historical verdict out of it is a case of the instrument supplying the conclusion. The pull is bidirectional and must be named as such: an isolated northwestern outlier can be talked up as a relict of an early northwestern distribution, or talked up as a recent arrival. Neither follows from the scatter, and the prestige-bias and preferred-counter-narrative tests both bite here.
affected_claims: DMB-001 (superseded), DMB-005; and every claim that treats Brahui's position as evidence in either direction, including IH-135 / H-01
correction: Unit 2 measures the thing the statistic could not see. Exclusive cognate sharing across Brahui, Kurukh and Malto is computed from a retrieved cognate-coded Dravidian dataset (SRC-049) and reported against every other pair and triple in the same dataset (DMB-017 to DMB-022), so the subgroup is measured rather than assumed. The contested status of the subgroup is recorded separately at DMB-023 to DMB-026 rather than folded into the measurement.
future_control: Any measurement over two or more languages in this repository states, in the claim row itself, whether it assumes the languages are independent observations, and if the languages are claimed to be related it names the tree it assumed or records that it used none. Any planar distance over geographic coordinates reports the great-circle distance alongside it, or is not reported.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: The same reaudit targets as BF-005: RA-004 for DME-023's unstated geographic reference, RA-005 for the inherited Brahui rows. Additionally, no earlier work in this repository has ever used a phylogenetic assumption, so there is no prior tree-based claim to reaudit; that absence is itself why the control above is written as a positive requirement rather than a correction.

topic: A retrieved passage carrying demonstrably wrong bibliographic metadata
failed_output: The first draft of DMM-007 cited the 195-item North Dravidian word count and the conclusion that a three-language northern group is 'doubtful' as Digby 1973, BSOAS - because that is the record Consensus attached the passage to.
bias_or_method_failure: Treating a connector's bibliographic head as the source's identity. The passage is a review of a Kurux or Malto etymological work; the record is Simon Digby's review of Pratapaditya Pal ed., Aspects of Indian Art, an art-history volume the passage cannot be about. BSOAS bundles many reviews under one record and the head identifies only the first. Citing it as Digby 1973 would have put a fabricated attribution into a register, with a locator that resolves to the wrong thing - the exact failure mode the locator rule exists to prevent.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That a well-known indexing service returns metadata bound to the text it returns. For journals that bundle reviews it does not, and the failure is silent: the passage is real, the citation is plausible, and nothing in the output flags the mismatch.
affected_claims: DMM-007; and by extension every claim in this unit sourced through SRC-053, which is most of them
correction: DMM-007 is capped at PROVISIONAL and its source row SRC-064 is named 'Unattributed BSOAS review passage', with access_status ATTRIBUTION_UNRESOLVED. The passage is quoted and its author, date and reviewed work are all recorded as unknown. Nothing is inferred from the wrong head.
future_control: Before citing any connector-returned passage, check that its content is about what its title says. Where a record is a review, an editorial or a bundled item, treat the head as unverified until the passage's own subject matches it. Standing policy question raised at D-040.

topic: A genetic null read as corroborating a lexical null
failed_output: A draft interpretation paired DMM-020 (no signal of Oraon-related ancestry in the Brahui) with DMM-004 (Brahui's exclusive lexical sharing with Kurux and with Malto is at chance) and read the two together as convergent evidence that the North Dravidian upper node is weak.
bias_or_method_failure: Using living people as linguistic fossils, which constitution §4.M names as this domain's trap, and collapsing two of the four histories the same section requires be kept apart. Modern genetics does not date or subgroup a language. The convergence is also illusory in its own terms: a lexical null and a genetic null are nulls in different systems, and Singh et al. themselves offer admixture loss as an explanation, which would make the genetic null uninformative about descent even within genetics.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That two independent-looking results pointing the same way strengthen each other. Here they are not measuring the same object, so agreement is not corroboration - the same error as counting two citations of one source as two sources, moved from bibliography into evidence classes.
correction: DMM-020 is filed strictly under speaker ancestry with the prohibition on its face. DMI-009 states that neither genetic result bears on subgrouping in either direction, and quotes a population-genetics paper stating the same against its own subject matter. DMG-5 carries an explicit warning that a genetic null looks like its prediction and does not confirm it.
future_control: No claim may cite a genetic result and a linguistic result as joint support for one proposition. Where both exist they get separate rows in separate histories, and any bridge between them is a distinct claim tested under step 10.

topic: A parse check mistaken for independent confirmation
failed_output: A draft of DMM-006 presented the reproduction of Kobayashi and Tirkey's 515 and 175, and the review passage's 195, as three independent confirmations of the Kurux-Malto subgroup.
bias_or_method_failure: Those are counts taken FROM DEDR by other scholars, re-taken from a re-encoding of DEDR. The agreement tests whether the file parses faithfully; it cannot test the claim, because there is only ever one source. Presenting it as confirmation would have breached the source-independence constraint while appearing to satisfy it - the near-exactness of the match is what makes the error attractive.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That a number reproduced from an independent publication is independent evidence. It is independent of this session's arithmetic and not of the underlying dictionary.
correction: DMM-006's claim text and notes state that it verifies the instrument and nothing else. DEP-013 records the relationship. DMI-006 states that this unit is not an independent replication of PR #16 either, since DravLex and DEDR descend from the same judgements (DEP-012, DEP-015).
future_control: When a measurement reproduces a published number, ask first whether the publication took its number from the same source being measured. If it did, the result is a parse check with an answer key and must be labelled as one.
